clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old man with a history of IgG4 lung disease and positive ANCA/PR3 antibody presented with 3 weeks of progressive productive cough, haemoptysis, myalgias, arthralgias, weakness, fever, and chills. On admission, he was febrile, tachycardic, tachypneic, hypotensive, and hypoxic with moderate respiratory distress and diffuse crackles on lung exam. Chest CT showed a marked increase in diffuse lung opacities, nodules, and masses. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) confirmed copious blood in the airways, indicating pulmonary hemorrhage, leading to intubation for hypoxic respiratory failure. A renal biopsy was also performed.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with haemoptysis and progressive respiratory symptoms.
Physical exam showed signs of respiratory distress and hypoxia.
Chest CT showed marked interval increase in diffuse lung opacities, nodules, and masses.
Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) revealed copious blood, confirming pulmonary hemorrhage.
Patient had a known history of positive ANCA and anti-proteinase 3 (PR3) antibodies.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: The acute worsening of respiratory symptoms, confirmed pulmonary hemorrhage, and implied renal involvement (renal biopsy performed) suggest a more aggressive vasculitic process like GPA, which is distinct from IgG4-related disease, despite the patient's prior diagnosis of IgG4 lung disease.

remaining_uncertainties: Specific pathology findings from the renal biopsy.
Current PR3-ANCA antibody titer at the time of this acute presentation (only prior levels were documented).
